title: AhnLab ASEC: Q-Dir and DesktopOK installers on the official SoftwareOK site were tampered with to install a Python RAT
date_note: ASEC's post is dated 26 November and gives no earlier disclosure day; its figures are dated 23 November.
summary: AhnLab's ASEC reports that some Q-Dir and DesktopOK installers on the official SoftwareOK website were tampered with to download a Python-based remote access trojan, including during updates of existing installs. Confirmed versions are Q-Dir 12.83.0.0, 12.84.0.0 and 12.85.0.0, and DesktopOK 12.82.0.0 and 12.85.0.0. ASEC says the cause and path of the replacement are not identified and notes Chinese-language comments in the code.
plain: AhnLab says some Q-Dir and DesktopOK installers from the official site were altered to install a remote-access trojan. The way they were changed has not been identified.
exec: AhnLab says official installers of two Windows utilities were altered to install a remote-access trojan; the cause is not identified.
action: AhnLab advises verifying SHA-256 hashes against the official page, uninstalling Q-Dir or DesktopOK and reinstalling a verified version, then checking for suspicious Python environments and scheduled tasks.
geo_basis: none: the sources give no location for the victim or the site's operator

sources.name: AhnLab ASEC: Software Supply Chain Attack via the Official SoftwareOK Website: Tampering with Q-Dir and DesktopOK Installation Files
